title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (Longue Marche continuation, 1981, pp. 650bis–787): Grothendieck is sketching the axioms for an integral 'Lie tower' attached to a Teichmüller–Galois structure. The data are discrete groups (Π, 𝔖, M, with Π_0 a finite-index or 'arithmetic' part, e.g. a Teichmüller modular group, or SL(2,Z) in genus 1). These are to be equipped with affine group schemes Π, 𝔖, M over S_0 = Spec Z whose Q-fibres play the role of algebraic hulls. The previous page considers all homomorphisms k_i from the 'Dehn twist' group T_0 ≅ Z to Π_0, conjugated by elements of Π_0. They extend to Lie homomorphisms Lie(k_i^!): T_0 ≅ Z → Lie(Π), assumed to be 'universal monomorphisms'. He concludes that Lie(Π) is generated as a Z-module by the Π_0-conjugates of the images of a generator of T_0.

This page globalises that infinitesimal statement. As a sheaf of groups on the big étale site of Spec Z, the identity component Π° is generated by a finite sequence (repetitions allowed) of subgroups k'_i(G_0). Here G_0 is the one-parameter group scheme extending T_0, essentially G_a, the unipotent hull of Z. Equivalently, Π is generated by these subgroups, which are permuted by conjugation, together with the constant group (Π_0)_{S_0}. Model case: the image of the mapping class group in Sp_{2g} is generated by symplectic transvections, the images of Dehn twists. Each transvection lies in a one-parameter unipotent subgroup G_a → Sp_{2g}, and Sp_{2g,Z} is generated by such root subgroups.

He then asks for a presentation. Do the relations of Π_0, plus the commutativity of square (57), suffice? Square (57) identifies the discrete T_0 → Π_0 with the restriction of the algebraic T_0 → Π via the canonical maps. Put differently, is Π the sheaf-theoretic amalgam of (Π_0)_{S_0} with copies of G_a along Z?

(58) imposes a second condition on the component groups γ_Π = Π/Π°, γ_𝔖 = 𝔖/𝔖°, γ_M = M/M°. They should be constant finite group schemes over Z, equal to the constant schemes of the finite component groups over Q. These finite groups are quotients of the discrete groups Π, 𝔖, M. The next page continues: the γ's fit into exact sequences (61), which allows defining the groups Π^Δ(Ẑ) etc. and factorisations Π → Π^Δ(Ẑ).
errors: No outright error. The generation statement is a hypothesis/desideratum, not a theorem. On the previous page Grothendieck himself flags that it seems unreasonable for Π_0 = SL(2,Z). This is consistent with later knowledge: SL(2,Z) is virtually free, and its relative/algebraic completion is far from being generated by finitely many G_a's with finite-type relations.

The presentation question (57) is left open. It is not true in general that a group scheme generated by root-type subgroups has only the 'obvious' relations: Steinberg-type relations among the G_a's are needed beyond the relations of the discrete group. So the naive answer 'relations of Π_0 plus (57)' is doubtful as stated.

ideas.what: Integral group scheme model over Spec Z of the algebraic hull of a (Teichmüller) modular group, with identity component generated as a big-étale sheaf by one-parameter unipotent subgroups extending Dehn twists
ideas.modern_name: Integral models of relative/Zariski completions of mapping class groups; generation of Sp_{2g,Z} by transvection root subgroups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Relative completion: Deligne, Hain (1990s); generation by transvections: classical (Dickson, Steinberg)
ideas.where_published: Only the general 'tour de Lie'/Teichmüller tower programme is hinted at in Esquisse d'un programme; this integral formulation appears unpublished

ideas.what: Asking whether Π is presented by the relations of the discrete group Π_0 plus compatibility of the Z → G_a extensions (square 57)
ideas.modern_name: Amalgamated/pushout presentation of group sheaves; comparison with Steinberg presentations

ideas.what: Requiring component groups Π/Π° etc. to be constant finite group schemes over Z, matching those over Q, to define Π^Δ(Ẑ)
ideas.modern_name: Constant component group / good reduction of π_0 of an integral model

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates an integral (over Spec Z) version of the algebraic hull of a Teichmüller modular group. Its identity component is to be generated by finitely many conjugates of G_a's coming from Dehn twists, with a conjectural presentation (relations of Π_0 plus the compatibility squares). Hain-style relative completions are developed over Q, not as Z-group schemes with this kind of presentation.
missed.quote: ou encore que Π est engendré par les k'_i(G_0) ... et le groupe discret (Π_0)_{S_0}. ... suffit-il d'écrire les relations de Π_0, plus la commutativité de (57) ?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Integral structures on relative completions of mapping class groups are relevant to Z-structures on motivic/Teichmüller Lie algebras. The presentation question is a concrete, unaddressed test case, e.g. for the Torelli/symplectic quotient.

missed.claim: Together with the previous page's margin remark, the page implicitly predicts the dichotomy between g ≥ 2-type arithmetic groups (finitely generated by unipotent root subgroups) and SL(2,Z), whose algebraic hull is not of this finite type. Hain later made this precise: the relative completion of SL(2,Z) has a large prounipotent radical tied to modular forms.
missed.quote: cette hyp. semble déraisonnable dès qu'on a Π_0 = SL(2,Z)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical anticipation of the role of modular forms in the genus-1 Teichmüller tower (cf. Hain–Matsumoto universal mixed elliptic motives). Minor, since it is a remark rather than a result.

deep.surprise_reason: An interesting but sketchy programmatic page: integral Lie-tower axioms with an open presentation question. The ideas are natural in hindsight and partially parallel later relative-completion work. There is no finished result.
transcription_corrections: Diagram (57): the source group is T_0 (Dehn twist group, ≅ Z) and its underlined algebraic version, not Γ_0.
(58): the middle group is the script/fraktur 𝔖 (as on the next page), i.e. γ_𝔖 = 𝔖/𝔖°, not G/G°.

Line 2: the inserted phrase reads roughly 'une suite finie de sous-groupes (toute répétition possible d'un même = disons en sous-groupes)'; 'sous-groupes' is struck at line 3, then reinserted in the interlinear addition.
The parenthetical after (Π_0)_{S_0} reads '(Et il y a la question relativement d'expliciter les relations...'; the parenthesis closes after the '?' following diagram (57).
